newsitem.title: FINLAND: Weakening forestries, Nokia fall take Helsinki lower.
newsitem.headline: Weakening forestries, Nokia fall take Helsinki lower.

text.p: A three-day winning streak on the Finnish bourse came to a halt on Tuesday as a budding recovery in forest industry shares turned back into a fall, and amid ongoing profit-taking in telecoms blue-chip Nokia.
The HEX all-share index fell 0.7 percent to close at 2.354.28 with decliners leading advancers four to three in moderately active 480 million markka turnover.

After five days of cautious gains, forest shares shed nearly 2.5 percent on the sector sub-index with UPM-Kymmene, Europe's biggest forest industry company, down 3.10 markka, or 3.5 percent, to 89.40 markka.
Nokia fell 2.50 markka to 253.00 as investors took profits after last week's steep rise in the share. Nokia last week reported healthy third-quarter earnings.
Banking group Merita was heavily traded and ended unchanged at 14.40 markka after touching a 16-month high 14.60 markka.

Awaiting an EU Commission decision due on Wednesday, wholesaler and retailer Kesko eased 2.50 markka to 62.50 after hitting a five-month low 61.50 markka on reports that the commission will reject its merger with domestic rival Tuko.
